title: Phenotypic differences between interfertile Chlamydomonas species- timelapse microscopy data, part 1
author: Garcia III, Galo
license_note: Zenodo record metadata license field: cc-by-4.0

steps.title: Collect and suspend cells
steps.instruction: Harvest Chlamydomonas cells from agar plates and resuspend them in sterile water.

steps.title: Overnight incubation for gametes
steps.instruction: Leave the cell suspension undisturbed overnight to promote gamete formation; during this period non‑motile cells settle and motile cells remain in the supernatant.

steps.title: Enrich motile cells
steps.instruction: Carefully collect the supernatant containing the enriched motile cells without disturbing the settled non‑motile cells.

steps.title: Load cells into agar microchambers
steps.instruction: Introduce the enriched motile cells into agar microchambers that are 100 µm in diameter and 40 µm deep.

steps.title: Prepare microscope setup
steps.instruction: Configure the Nikon Ti2‑E microscope with a Photometrics Kinetix digital sCMOS camera and a Plan Apo 10× 0.45 Air objective; place a red‑light filter (IR long‑pass, 610 nm, ThorLabs) in the light path to maintain swimming behavior.

substeps.instruction: Mount the camera on the microscope.
Insert the IR long‑pass filter (610 nm) into the illumination path.

steps.title: Acquire timelapse DIC video
steps.instruction: Record differential interference contrast (DIC) videos with a 5.1 ms exposure, acquiring an image every 50 ms for a total duration of three minutes (resulting in 3601 frames at 20 fps, pixel size 0.6398 µm/pixel). Ensure the DIC polarizer is inserted; if omitted the data will be brightfield.

steps.title: Repeat experiment for consistency
steps.instruction: Perform the entire procedure four independent times to ensure reproducibility of the timelapse data.
